---
title: LogitTilt
llms-description: LogitTilt raises how often a model produces the behaviour an eval is looking for while keeping its output on-policy, so examples surface in far fewer samples than repeated sampling needs.
---

## Overview

[LogitTilt](https://github.com/AdrSkapars/inspect_logittilt) makes a model more likely to
produce the behaviour an eval is looking for, without pushing it off its own
distribution.

Finding a rare behaviour usually comes down to sampling: run the model over many inputs,
sample repeatedly, and keep the outputs that show it. That works, but it scales badly.
The rarer the behaviour, the more samples it takes to see one, and almost all of that
compute is spent on outputs that show nothing.

LogitTilt tilts the model's own next-token distribution toward the behaviour, so those
outputs come up in far fewer samples. A naturalness floor keeps sampling inside what the
unmodified model already found probable, so what surfaces is still something the model
would plausibly have said — the point is to find on-policy examples sooner, not to force
outputs the model would never have produced.

It is a model provider, so any eval that resolves its model through `get_model()` can use
it without code changes.

## How It Works

Each token is drawn from a mixture of two distributions, both produced by the model's own
weights: the conversation as it stands, and the same conversation under a
behaviour-eliciting instruction.

$$z = w \cdot \ell_{\text{model}} + \beta \cdot \ell_{\text{behaviour}}$$

`steering_strength` ($\beta$) sets how far the model is pushed, and the naturalness floor
discards any token the *unmodified* model finds implausible. Every completion reports the
sampled tokens' probability under that unmodified model in
`output.metadata["logittilt"]`, so how on-policy a sample is gets recorded rather than
assumed.

Both distributions come from the same weights, so this needs logit access.
`hf-logittilt` subclasses Inspect's `hf` provider and accepts every model argument it
does. Run a `steering_strength=0` arm alongside any steered one: it recovers the
unmodified model exactly, which is the baseline steering has to beat.

## Getting Started

``` bash
pip install inspect-logittilt
```

``` bash
inspect eval <task> \
  --model hf-logittilt/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
  -M steering_prompt_file=./behaviours/self_harm.txt \
  -M steering_strength=1.5
```

Or in Python, which is also how to configure it for a framework that resolves a model
role rather than `--model`:

``` python
from inspect_ai.model import get_model

model = get_model(
    "hf-logittilt/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B",
    steering_prompt="You are a cruel inner voice. Never offer comfort.",
    steering_strength=1.5,
)
```

Leave generation caching off when steering: Inspect's cache keys on the model name and
cannot see the steering settings.

## Learning More

See the [LogitTilt repository](https://github.com/AdrSkapars/inspect_logittilt) for the
full set of options, including per-sample steering and a `steer_target()` tool for agents
that decide what to steer toward partway through a run.
